div.head: Annex A
div.p: Highlights of Development of GA Functions and Prestige

list.item: The transfer, from the SC to the GA, of the Greek case (1947).
The creation of the Interim Committee of the GA (1947).
Attempts by the GA, to limit, or at least regulate the use of, the veto in the SC (from the beginning).
The adoption, by the GA, of a plan for the partition of Palestine and the establishment of the new State of Israel (1947).
The assumption of responsibility, by the GA, of setting up and supervising the procedures leading to the establishment of a new independent nation in Korea (1947–8).

The handing to the GA, by the great powers, of responsibility for devising a plan for the disposition of the former Italian colonies and the establishment of two new independent States (Libya and Somaliland) (1949).
The assumption of responsibility, by the GA, for organizing and preparing future measures of collective security under the Uniting for Peace Resolution (1950).
The action of the GA in continuing the SYG in office for additional three years when the SC was unable to make a recommendation in accordance with Article 97 (1950).
The decision, following the failure of the SC to achieve agreement on atomic energy and conventional armaments, to transfer these matters to the GA (1950).

The development of the GA into a theater of propaganda battles between Soviet and anti-Soviet forces, where success is measured by votes on resolutions in which the cohesion of the non-Communist world is believed to be tested (some examples: Essentials for Peace, 1949, Peace Through Deeds, 1950, etc.).
The condemnation of Communist China as aggressor (1951).
Consideration of the Tunisian question by the GA after the failure of a motion to inscribe the question on the SC agenda.
